record.content_text:
We measure angles in degrees. We use a protractor to measure an angle.

Protractor image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-005.png

Take note of the following when you use a protractor:

- A protractor has a centre, which can also be called the origin.
  Origin image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-006.png
  When you measure an angle you have to make sure that the centre (or origin) of the protractor is exactly on the vertex of the angle that you want to measure.

- The centre (or origin) of a protractor is on the base line of the protractor.
  Base line image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-007.png
  When you measure an angle you also have to make sure that one side of the base line of the protractor is exactly on one of the arms of the angle that you want to measure.

- There are two zeroes on a protractor.
  If you begin measuring from the zero on the left hand side of the protractor, you use the outer scale on the protractor.
  Outer-scale image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-008.png
  If you begin measuring from the zero on the right hand side of the protractor, you use the inner scale on the protractor.
  Inner-scale image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-009.png

record.content_text:
Different types of angles have different names. The names you may need to use when working with angles are given in the table below.

| Name of angle | Size of angle |
| --- | --- |
| acute angle | between $0^{\circ}$ and $90^{\circ}$ |
| right angle | $90^{\circ}$ |
| obtuse angle | between $90^{\circ}$ and $180^{\circ}$ |
| straight angle | $180^{\circ}$ |
| reflex angle | between $180^{\circ}$ and $360^{\circ}$ |
| revolution | $360^{\circ}$ |

record_links.rationale: This worked example measures a right angle.

heading_path.h3: Worked example 15.4: Measuring a right angle

record.evidence_quote: Use a protractor to measure the given angle in the diagram below. Diagram source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-010.png
record.prompt_text:
Use a protractor to measure the given angle in the diagram below.

Diagram source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-010.png
record.answer_text:
Step 1: Consider the diagram and estimate the size of the angle.

The diagram shows two arms: $AC$ and $AB$. It seems as if they form a right angle, which is shaded green. A right angle is equal to $90^{\circ}$.

Step 2: Place the protractor correctly on the angle.

Placement image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-011.png

- The centre of the protractor should be on the vertex of the angle.
- The base line of the protractor should be on one arm of the angle.

Step 3: Choose the scale you will use.

The arm on which the base line lies is to the right side of the protractor. On the right side, it is the inner scale that starts from 0, so use the inner scale.

Step 4: Read off the size of the angle from the protractor, and give the answer. Name the angle correctly, and remember to include the degree symbol.

$$
B\hat{A}C = 90^{\circ}
$$

heading_path.h3: Worked example 15.5: Measuring an acute angle

record.evidence_quote: Use a protractor to measure the marked angle shown below. Diagram source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-012.png
record.prompt_text:
Use a protractor to measure the marked angle shown below.

Diagram source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-012.png
record.answer_text:
Step 1: Consider the diagram and estimate the size of the angle.

The angle shaded red is between two arms: $PS$ and $PT$. It seems that the marked angle is an acute angle.

An acute angle is between $0^{\circ}$ and $90^{\circ}$. This angle is nearer to $90^{\circ}$ than to $0^{\circ}$.

Step 2: Place the protractor correctly on the angle.

Placement image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-013.png

- The centre of the protractor should be on the vertex of the angle.
- The base line of the protractor should be on one arm of the angle.

Step 3: Choose the correct scale.

The arm on which the base line lies is to the right side of the protractor, so use the inner scale.

Step 4: Read off the size of the angle from the protractor, and check against your estimation.

$67^{\circ}$ is an acute angle, and is closer to $90^{\circ}$ than to $0^{\circ}$.

Step 5: Name the angle, and give the answer.

$$
S\hat{P}T = 67^{\circ}
$$

Use the dotted lines shown to help with your estimation. The dotted lines have a $90^{\circ}$ angle between them.
record.answer_text:
Step 1: Consider the diagram and estimate the size of the angle.

The diagram shows two arms: $AB$ and $AC$. It seems as if they form an obtuse angle, which is shaded red.

An obtuse angle is between $90^{\circ}$ and $180^{\circ}$. This angle is almost a full straight angle, so it must be very close to $180^{\circ}$.

Step 2: Place the protractor correctly on the angle.

Placement image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-015.png

- The centre of the protractor should be on the vertex of the angle.
- The base line of the protractor should be on one arm of the angle.

Step 3: Choose the correct scale.

The arm on which the base line lies is to the right side of the protractor, so use the inner scale.

Step 4: Read off the size of the angle from the protractor, and check against your estimation.

$175^{\circ}$ is an obtuse angle, and is close to $180^{\circ}$.

Step 5: Name the angle, and give the answer.

$$
B\hat{A}C = 175^{\circ}
$$

heading_path.h3: Worked example 15.7: Measuring a reflex angle

record.evidence_quote: Use a protractor and measure the angle shown below. [Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-016.png]
record.prompt_text:
Use a protractor and measure the angle shown below.

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-016.png]
record.answer_text:
Step 1: Consider the diagram and estimate the size of the angle.

The diagram shows two arms: $XY$ and $XZ$. They form a reflex angle, which is shaded red.

A reflex angle is between $180^{\circ}$ and $360^{\circ}$. This angle is very near to $360^{\circ}$.

Step 2: Find a way to measure this reflex angle.

An ordinary protractor can only measure angles between $0^{\circ}$ to $180^{\circ}$. We cannot measure a reflex angle with an ordinary protractor. We have to measure the angle that is not shaded and then subtract the answer from $360^{\circ}$.

Step 3: Place the protractor correctly on the angle to measure.

[Protractor placement image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-017.png]

- The centre of the protractor should be on the vertex of the angle.
- The base line of the protractor should be on one arm of the angle.

Step 4: Choose the scale and read off the size of the angle.

The acute angle measures $18^{\circ}$.

Step 5: Subtract the measured angle from $360^{\circ}$ and give the correct answer. Check against your estimation, and name the reflex angle correctly.

Reflex $Z\hat{X}Y = 360^{\circ} - 18^{\circ} = 342^{\circ}$.

record_links.rationale: This hint explains how to measure reflex angles by subtracting from 360 degrees.

record.evidence_quote: Remember that reflex angles are always less than $360^{\circ}$, but more than $180^{\circ}$. A full turn or revolution is equal to $360^{\circ}$.
